pp:ee:2001:q1.title: GATE EE 2001 | Set 1 | Question: 1
pp:ee:2001:q1.question:
In a series RLC circuit at resonance, the magnitude of the voltage developed
across the capacitor
options: can never be greater than the input voltage

can be greater than the input voltage, however, it is $90^{\circ}$ out of phase with
the input voltage
can be greater than the input voltage, and is in phase with the input voltage.

detailed_solution.concept: Electric Circuits - Resonance and Locus Diagrams
detailed_solution.markdown:
In a series RLC circuit, at resonance

$V_L=jQV_{source}$ and  $V_c=-jQV_{source}$

also for  $Q \gt 1, |V_c| \gt |V_{source}|$

Hence, option (C) is correct.

pp:ee:2001:q3.title: GATE EE 2001 | Set 1 | Question: 3
pp:ee:2001:q3.question:
A unit step voltage is applied at t = 0 to a series RL circuit with zero initial
conditions.
options: It is possible for the current to be oscillatory.
The voltage across the resistor at t = $0^{+}$ is zero.
The energy stored in the inductor in the steady state is zero.
The resistor current eventually falls to zero.

detailed_solution.concept: Electric Circuits - Transients and Steady State Response
detailed_solution.markdown: At $t=0^+$ inductor works as open circuit. Hence, complete source voltage drops across it and consequently, current through the resistor R is zero. Hence, voltage across the resistor at $t=0^+$ is zero. And further with time it rises accroding to $V_R(t)=(1-e^{-Rt/L})u(t)$.

pp:ee:2001:q15.title: GATE EE 2001 | Set 1 | Question: 15
pp:ee:2001:q15.question:
Given the homogeneous state-space equaion
$$\dot{x}=\begin{bmatrix} -3 &1 \\ 0&-2 \end{bmatrix}x$$
the steady state value $x_{ss}=\lim_{t\rightarrow \infty }x(t)$, given the initial state value of $x\left ( t \right )=\left [ 10-10 \right ]^{T}$, is

detailed_solution.markdown:
$$[sI-A]^{-1}=\begin{bmatrix} s+3 &-1 \\ 0 & s+2 \end{bmatrix}^{-1} =\begin{bmatrix} \frac{1}{s+3} &\frac{1}{(s+2)(s+3)} \\ 0& \frac{1}{s+2} \end{bmatrix}$$

$$e^{At}=L^{-1}[sI-A]^{-1}=\begin{bmatrix} e^{-3t} & e^{-2t}-e^{-3t}\\ 0 & e^{-2t} \end{bmatrix}$$

$$x(t)=e^{At}X(0) =\begin{bmatrix} e^{-3t} & e^{-2t}-e^{-3t}\\ 0 & e^{-2t} \end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix} 10\\ -10 \end{bmatrix}$$

$$\therefore \;\; x(t)=\begin{bmatrix} 20e^{-3t}-10e^{-2t}\\ -10e^{-2t} \end{bmatrix}$$

$$\therefore \;\; X_{ss}=\lim_{t \rightarrow \infty }\begin{bmatrix} 0\\ 0 \end{bmatrix}$$

pp:ee:2001:q34.title: GATE EE 2001 | Set 1 | Question: 34
pp:ee:2001:q34.question: A star-connected 440 V, 50 Hz alternators has per phase synchronous reactance of 10$\Omega$. It supplies a balanced capacitive load current of 20 A, as shown in the per phase equivalent circuit of figure. It is desirable to have zero voltage regulation. The load power factor should be

detailed_solution.markdown:
$$\begin{aligned}

E_f\angle \delta &= V\angle 0+I_a\angle \phi \cdot Z_s\angle \theta  \\

&= V\angle 0+I_aZ_s\angle \phi + \theta\;\;...(i)

\end{aligned}$$

Squaring both side, we get,

$|E_f|=|V|^2+|I_a|^2|Z_s|^2+2 |V||I_a||Z_s| \cos (\theta +\phi )$

For zero regulation, $|E_f|=|V|$

$$\begin{aligned}

\Rightarrow \; \cos (\theta +\phi ) &= -\frac{|I_a||Z_s|}{2|V|}\\

&= -\frac{20 \times 10}{2 \times \frac{440}{\sqrt{3}}}\\

&= -0.3936\\

\theta +\phi &= 113.178^{\circ}\\

\phi  &= 113.178^{\circ}-90^{\circ} \\

&= 23.178^{\circ}\\

\cos \phi &= 0.9192

\end{aligned}$$

pp:ee:2001:q48.title: GATE EE 2001 | Set 1 | Question: 48
pp:ee:2001:q48.question: An n-channel JFET, having a pinch-off voltage ($V_{p}$) of -5 V, shows a transconductance ($g_{m}$) of 1 mA/V when the applied gate-to-source voltage ($V_{GS}$) is -3V. Its maximum transconductance (in mA/V) is

primary.subtopicLabel: BJT, FET and their Biasing Circuits

detailed_solution.concept: Analog Electronics - BJT, FET and their Biasing Circuits
detailed_solution.markdown:
$g_m=-\frac{2I_{DSS}}{V_p}\left ( 1-\frac{V_{GS}}{V_p} \right )$

$1 \; mA/V=-\frac{2I_{DSS}}{5} \left( 1-\frac{-3}{-5} \right ) =\frac{2}{5}\times \left( 1-\frac{3}{5} \right )I_{DSS}$

$\Rightarrow \; \; I_{DSS}=\left ( \frac{5}{2} \right )^2 \; mA$

$(g_{m})_{max}=-\frac{2I_{DSS}}{V_p}=-\frac{2 \times 25}{4 \times (-5)}=2.5 \; mA/V$

pp:ee:2001:q49.question: A half-wave thyristor converter supplies a purely inductive load, as shown in figure. If the triggering angle of the thyristor is $120^{\circ}$, the extinction angle will be

detailed_solution.markdown: $$\begin{aligned} V_m \sin \omega t&=L\frac{di}{dt}\\ \frac{di}{dt}&=\frac{V_m}{L} \sin \omega t\\ \int_{0}^{i}di&=\frac{V_m}{L} \int_{\alpha }^{t}\sin \omega t\; dt\\ i&=\frac{V_m}{\omega L} \cos \omega t|_t^\alpha \\ i&=\frac{V_m}{\omega L} (\cos \alpha -\cos \omega t)\;\;...(i)\\ \text{For extinction angle, at }&\omega t=\beta ,i=0\\ \Rightarrow \;0&=\frac{V_m}{\omega L} (\cos \alpha -\cos \beta )\\ \text{Which gives, }& \cos \alpha = \cos \beta \\ \beta &=2 n \pi \pm \alpha \\ \text{For, } n&=1\\ \beta &=240^{\circ},480^{\circ} \end{aligned}$$

pp:ee:2001:q50.title: GATE EE 2001 | Set 1 | Question: 50
pp:ee:2001:q50.question: A single-phase full-bridge voltage source inverter feeds a purely inductive load, a shown in figure, where $T_{1}$, $T_{2}$, $T_{3}$, $T_{4}$ are power transistors and $D_{1}$, $D_{2}$, $D_{3}$, $D_{4}$ are feedback diodes. The inverter is operated in square-wave mode with a frequency of 50 Hz. If the average load current is zero, what is the time duration of conduction of each feedback diode in a cycle?

detailed_solution.markdown: Conduction time $=\frac{T}{4}=\frac{20}{4}=5 \; ms$
